documents.title: Agent for Service of Process — Duties and Change of Agent Information Sheet
documents.description: Explains who is eligible to serve as a California agent for service of process (a resident individual or a registered corporate agent under Corp. Code section 1505), the certificate a corporation must file to become a registered corporate agent, the separate statutory mechanisms for an entity to change its own agent after formation (a current Statement of Information, not a distinct filing) and for an agent to resign on its own initiative, and the consequences when no valid agent can be found. Distinct from this corpus's existing formation documents, which cover only the initial agent designation.

fields.label: Prior agent's name
fields.whyWeAsk: The agent currently on file with the Secretary of State who is being replaced -- naming them is what makes this a change, not a first-time designation.

fields.label: New agent's name
fields.whyWeAsk: The person or corporate agent taking over as agent for service of process. California only recognizes two eligible categories -- a California resident, or a corporation separately registered as a 1505 agent -- see the eligibility clause above.

fields.label: New agent's California street address
fields.whyWeAsk: Required only when the new agent is an individual, not a corporate agent -- a corporate agent's own address is already on file with the Secretary of State, which is why this field is optional here.

fields.label: Name of person preparing this information sheet

Code § 17942), owed in addition to the flat $800 minimum franchise tax by an LLC taxed as a partnership or disregarded entity: who it applies to, the tiered fee schedule, the gross-income (not net-profit) definition of "total income," and the mid-year estimate-and-payment requirement.

documents.title: Corporate Board Resolution / Action by Written Consent
documents.description: The actual statutory mechanics for a corporation's board (or shareholders) to act without holding a meeting -- unanimous written consent for the board, versus a meeting-equivalent (not unanimous) vote count for most shareholder action, plus the meeting-notice-and-waiver alternative and the limits on delegating authority to a committee. Distinct from this project's Corporate Bylaws and Articles of Incorporation documents, which don't cover the mechanics of taking a specific action.

documents.title: Corporate Dissolution (Certificate of Dissolution)
documents.description: The separately-codified process for dissolving a California for-profit corporation, distinct from the LLC Dissolution and Cancellation document's LLC-specific scheme: shareholder-vote grounds, the certificate of election and certificate of dissolution filings, winding-up commencement and director powers, distribution priority, surviving claims against the dissolved corporation and its shareholders, and Franchise Tax Board minimum-tax clearance.

documents.title: Employer Identification Number (EIN) — Information Sheet
documents.description: Explains the federal Employer Identification Number: its statutory and regulatory basis, which entities and individuals the IRS says need one, situations where a single-member LLC or sole proprietor may continue using an existing number instead of a new EIN, how an application is made (including the IRS's own free-of-charge warning), a common point of confusion about whether a business reorganization requires a new EIN, and how California's separate EDD payroll tax account number differs from the federal EIN.

documents.title: Fictitious Business Name (DBA) Statement — Information Sheet
documents.description: An informational sheet describing California's county-level (not state-level) requirement to file a fictitious business name statement when using a name other than a registrant's true legal name. Covers the statutory definition by registrant type, the 40-day filing deadline and county of filing, required content, the newspaper publication requirement, 5-year expiration, the limited rebuttable presumption of exclusive use it creates, and the civil/criminal consequences of noncompliance.

documents.title: Founders' Agreement

documents.title: General Partnership Agreement

documents.title: Multi-Member LLC Operating Agreement
